chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: A dance of continuous applause and a singing-dancing medley
summary: He strung only the best applause-getting steps together without time-step breathers, and wanted to blend singing and dancing in one medley.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You said there are some other things you wanted to do. What are you talking about?
You said there are some other things you also wanted to do, you'll get around to it some day. What are you referring to?
Referring to doing a medley of dancing and singing in one. Not to say I dance and then sing and then sing and then dance, but to sing and dance when it's a medley, which I've always tried to do.

No. I did something else nobody had ever done, too. I would do a step and the step is good and the audience would applaud. Then I'd do a time step as a breather and then you do another step, and if it's good, the audience will applaud. So

I took all the good steps the audience applauded on and put them together. Do you understand what I'm saying? And took the time step out, there's no breather. There's step after step after step after step -- applause, applause, applause after applause. Do you understand? There was no letup on the applause. I would start out there and wind up over here and the audience is applauding from the time I start there to the time I go here, and I'm finished. You understand? I did about five or six steps between that side of the stage to this side. And applause all the way across and I'm going off the stage and the dance is finished. See what I mean?
That's right. That's right. And I come back and give them more, another style.
